pages:
Two little pots on the booth table.
Somebody keeps them watered.

Same seedling, two pots. One sits by
a violet shard, one by a firefly jar.

Side by side, they look identical.
For now.

Nothing's changed since this morning.
Plants keep their own hours.

The shard pot leans, like it's tired.
The jar pot has put out a new leaf.

Nothing's changed since this morning.
Plants keep their own hours.

The jar pot is thriving. A bead of
water rests on one leaf.

Lean in and it hums. Two low notes,
like a river a long way off.

Nothing's changed since this morning.
Plants keep their own hours.

She paints over the catalogue numbers
cut from company flyers.

Your team's names go up one by one.
{lead} watches its name dry.

She paints over the catalogue numbers
cut from company flyers.

Behind {lead}'s name she adds a
faint colour. Not violet. Its own.

Decks, a crate of records, and a
sticky note: "FIVE notes, not four."
Four notes. Then nothing.

Each time the tune stops short,
{lead} turns toward the river.

The decks are quiet. He only plays
that tune from dusk onward.

A cork board buried in notes. Pins,
string, and a lot of question marks.

The bouncer pins up the page.
It's a drift chart.

Bonded creatures marked warm. Unbound
ones, cold. Pencil on the back:
"Signal strongest downstream?"

Someone also rated the snow.
Four out of ten. Crunchy.

The bouncer weighs the bag in one
hand, then pins the label up.

"Tidewater. River mouth.
More every month."

The bouncer pins up the page. Rows
of times, and violet lights at sea.

Every entry ends the same way:
"Sailed upstream at the river mouth."

The petition's full. Greenhouse, dock,
annex, field, bog, beach...
...lighthouse, forge. And one more.

At the bottom, a print nobody saw
anyone leave. Round. Smooth.
Like a river stone.

Crates stamped GREYSTONE,
stacked higher than a house.

You count the crates. Then you
count them again.

There are more here than the
cargo log admits to.
One crate, set apart from the rest.

This one's damp. River silt is
packed into the corners.

Funny. Greystone is dry rock
all the way down.

Crates in, crates out. Nobody asks
what's in them. Or asks me anything.

A crate of glass crystals. Pretty,
nearly violet. Not quite.

A woman buys one and clips it to
her creature's collar.

It looks fitted. It isn't. She pays
and walks off fast, smiling.

Lucky crystals! Made of glass.
Very lucky. Extremely glass.

A crack in the rock, violet behind it.
Quiet, for now.

A crack in the rock. Behind it,
violet crystal.

Behind the crystal: water, moving.
Your lantern dims, then holds.

The rock is still. Odric said it only
breathes at night.

An old ore cart. Somebody left in a
hurry, and didn't take the ore.
A plain stone. No name on it yet.

You set a small stone among
the others.

For the one that warned him
anyway.

ivo_miner.name: Odric
pages:
Twenty years I dug Greystone.
Now I come here. It's quieter.

A shutter between the racks.
RECALIBRATION. STAFF ONLY.

The box holds carry-cases. Each tag:
TINT DRIFT. RECALIBRATE.

You leave them by the door. A hand
takes them in. The shutter drops.
The window looks down on the river.
The window looks down on the river.

A dark tide line marks the bank,
well above the water.

I've dusted this place since before
it had a name on the door.

That picture? The Unbound would give
their eyeteeth for what's underneath.
Not that I'd know. I just dust it.

A banner hangs over a painting.
Plaque: "Where it all began."

You lift a corner. A vast river
creature, the founder kneeling by it.

Its brow crystal is cracked. Eyes
shut. Not sleeping. Hurting.

The guard's watching. Better to come
back after dark.

Annex. Staff and visitors only.
You're... a visitor. Fine.

Tanks of clear water, all empty.
Labelled: "DRIFT UNITS".

First week at the annex.
Everyone here walks very fast.

REVIVAL TECH - HEIGHTS ANNEX
Deliveries round the front.

Found this frozen near the pass.
A page from that field team, I think.

The edge of the field. The barrier
shine glows on the horizon.

The barrier shine spills gold over
the grass.

A Halovy lands on the fence. It turns
its back to the shine, toward the river.

Nan said dawn. The shine's best
first thing.

Lovely morning. The barrier shine's
up early again.
Tall reeds. The water sits low here.

Crate tracks in the mud. Company
boot prints.

The bog water here is lower than
anywhere else.

Census. Every creature counted,
every week. It's soothing. Usually.

Dark water round a little islet.
Very still.

You sit. Nobody speaks. The water
turns gold for one breath.

A Riverglint flashes once, nose
upstream. Then it's gone.

The angler said dusk. Nothing stirs
here till the light goes gold.

A wind chime of sea glass hangs
from the lamp post.

Violet glass on string. The breeze
knocks it about.

For a moment it rings four notes
you know. Then it's noise again.

Low tide's the best time.
The sea gives things back.
A buoy bobbing past the breakers.

A creature surfaces by the buoy.
No crystal. None at all.

A big wave spooks it under. Then it
comes back to the lifeguard. Alone.

Your partner hangs back from the
water. Maybe once it trusts you more.

In mine, its crystal's cracking.
And it's angry. Not sad.

It didn't want help, Cal.
It wanted out.

Fresh bread, warm stones.
Well. Warm-ish stones.

My baking stones used to stay warm
till lunch. Now they're cold by nine.

Ever since that kiln opened. Not
saying anything. I'm saying nine.
The old forge. Still warm, somehow.

Heat rises from deep under the town,
slow, like something asleep.

In it, faint, the same four river
notes. Even down here.

Just warm brick for now. The smith
said to come back at night.

start:
Same seedling, grown twice. One by a
shard, one by a firefly jar.

Look in on them once a day for three
days? Tell me what you see, not think.
in_progress:
Once a day. Plants don't care how
keen you are.
turn_in: The jar one thrived. Huh.

One pair of pots isn't science.
I won't claim more than that.

Here, a mossplum shake. Seemed right
to pay you in something green.

start:
Company flyers give every creature a
number. I give them their names back.

Lend me your team's for the wall?
The poster by the door.
turn_in: There. Names, not numbers.

I left the last space blank. For the
big one in the river. Whoever it is.

start:
Got my records back. Still can't
finish the phrase. It needs five.

I only ever get four. Come by after
dark and watch what your partner does.
turn_in: It turned to the river? Every time?

I heard it once, under the water.
Like something calling for help.

My guess? The company signal jams
the fifth note. Have this record.

start: Can you count crates? Quietly?

The Greystone ones. The log never
matches. I need a second pair of eyes.
turn_in: More than they declare. Knew it.
Don't say I asked. I like my job.

Here. Trail mix and a bit of gold.
Nobody counts those either.

start:
Name's Odric. I quit Greystone. The
deep seam breathed. You could hear it.

There's a way down from B1, past the
bottom pool. Go by night. See the crack.
in_progress:
Night. The seam only breathes
at night.
turn_in:
Water. Behind the crystal.
So I wasn't losing my mind.

The creatures digging with me were
fitted. They couldn't flinch.

One did anyway. Thanks for the stone.
Take these lantern moths.

start:
Want a secret? My glass sells best to
folk who can't stand the real thing.
Watch the stall a while. You'll see.
turn_in:
See? It passes for fitted when the
inspectors look. That's all it does.

Don't call me brave. I'm not.
I sell glass. Here, have one.

start:
Could you run this box to the annex?
Recalibration door. "Drift units."

Don't ask me what drift is.
I started on Monday.
turn_in:
Thanks. Did they say what
recalibration actually is?

No? Okay. Here's some gold for
the legwork.

You can see the river from up there,
right? Gran says it used to be higher.

start:
Company rule: report anyone staring
at the founder's picture too long.

You can look. One second.
I'm bored, not cruel.
turn_in:
One second, I said. Fine.
It's a good picture.

Plaque says "Where it all began."
Nobody ever asks where that was.

start:
Found this frozen near the pass.
A page from that field team, I think.

The Firefly lot keep a board for
things like this. Would you take it?
turn_in:
Pinned up? Good. Someone should read
it who isn't a glacier.

Calm tea, for the walk down. Warms
you better than my company does.

start:
That barrier shine gets brighter
every season. As more get fitted.

And the river gets lower. I just
count seasons. Come look at dawn.
turn_in:
My Tumbloams got out once. A wild
Enraged one hurt the smallest.

Wild is hard, I know. That doesn't
make the shine kind. Seeds, for you.

start:
The count drops every week. Same
reeds. Same weekday.

Would you look over those reeds? I
follow rules. I want to know which.
turn_in: Taken for "catalogue". Of course.

This week my report lists names, not
numbers. One rule broken. Once.

I'm rather proud of it. Take a
reading sheet. Count for yourself.

start:
There's a fish that only shows where
the river beast once rested.

By the dark islet, at dusk. Sit still
and you might catch sight of it.
turn_in: Upstream. It always points upstream.

The old folk called the river beast
"the one who keeps the light".

My gran's drawing. Don't say a word.
Just nod.

start:
My best sea glass comes up violet
now. More of it every month.

It's washing out of the river mouth.
The river's bleeding, if you ask me.

The Firefly lot wanted some, for
evidence. Take them this bag?
turn_in:
Thank you. The river's been trying to
tell someone for a while.

Keep this charm. It rings like the
tide coming in.

start: Watching the water. Nothing to see.

Come back to the buoy with a partner
that trusts you. Then maybe.
turn_in:
No crystal. Never had one.
It came back because it wanted to.

You didn't see that. Here,
a droplet charm. Go on now.

start:
I keep two logs. One's the weather.
One's violet lights out at sea.

Company boats with crates, I'd say.
Take a page to The Firefly?
turn_in:
I can call a storm three days out.
People, never.

Have my spare lure lantern. Fish
like it more than they like me.

start:
Don't laugh. I've been having the
river dream too.

Sit down. Kettle's on. I'll tell it
once and then we're done.
turn_in:
Right. That's enough feelings for
one bin day.

start:
Forges are cooling since Revival Tech
put a crystal kiln next door.

I never fit crystals to my forge
creatures. Feel the old forge at night.
turn_in:
Grandad said the old one under the
mountain dreams.

If it dreams of that river creature's
pain, the signal reaches everywhere.

Tell the Firefly lot they've a friend
at the anvil. Take this ember charm.

start:
Last thing. A petition. Everyone
you've helped, every town.

It's not one rebel. It's ordinary
folk. Let's show that.
in_progress:
Every town. Everyone you helped.
Then leave it on the board overnight.
turn_in:
Everyone signed. Even... whoever
left that print.

New poster for the wall:
WE ASKED. NOW WE GO.

Keep the bell. Ring it when
it's time.
